title: One Perfect Scene: Mad Men - Shut the Door, Have a Seat
summary: This video breaks down a pivotal scene from Mad Men Season 3, Episode 13, titled "Shut the Door. Have a Seat." It analyzes how the characters navigate a high-stakes corporate takeover and corporate conspiracy, shifting from desperate conflict to calculated alignment.
key_points: The scene takes place 15 minutes into the Season 3 finale, "Shut the Door. Have a Seat."
Sterling Cooper has been bought by British agency Putnam, Powell, and Lowe (PPL) and is slated to be absorbed into McCann Erickson.
Don Draper refuses to give up creative control and become a mid-level cog at McCann.
Bert Cooper insists on bringing in Roger Sterling because of his relationship with American Tobacco, their biggest client.
The partners offer to buy back Sterling Cooper from PPL for the purchase price plus 12 percent, but Lane Price rejects it because he believes only Sterling Cooper is being sold while PPL remains.
Lane Price realizes later on a call with London that PPL is also being sold, meaning he too will be absorbed into McCann.
The partners need to secure 12 million dollars worth of business in less than 72 hours to pull off the buyback.
They decide to poach accounts completely unnoticed by their bosses across the pond.
Lane Price holds all the power as the only one who can fire them, and they negotiate to make him a partner.
